name: Tycho
description: A young impact basin with bright ejecta rays that stretch 1,500 – 2,600 km (around 1,600 miles) across the lunar surface.

name: Copernicus
description: A massive, highly visible lunar impact crater with terraced walls and a central peak, located in the eastern Mare Imbrium region.

name: Kepler
description: A classic rayed crater located between the Oceanus Procellarum and Mare Insularum, forming a well-known triad with Copernicus and Aristarchus.

name: Clavius
description: One of the largest and oldest crater formations on the near side, notable for its vast plain and smaller overlapping crater chains.

name: Aristotoles
description: A prominent, well-preserved lunar impact crater located in the northeastern quadrant of the Moon's near side along the southern edge of the Mare Frigoris (Sea of Cold).

name: Eudoxus
description: A prominent lunar impact crater featuring a terraced interior rim, level floor and a cluster of central low hills composed of pure crystalline plagioclase.

name: Plato
description: A large lava-filled impact crater known for its dark, smooth floor that stands out against the brighter surrounding mountainous rim. It is located on the northeastern shore of the Mare Imbrium (Sea of Showers).

name: Archimedes
description: An ancient lava-filled impact crater with a smooth dark floor and surrounding crater walls that stand tall above the eastern edge of the Mare Imbrium (Sea of Showers).

name: Gassendi
description: A large, complex impact crater located at the northern edge of the Mare Humorum (Sea of Moisture). Its fractured lava-filled floor contains several central peaks that rise to a height of 1.2km.

name: Bullialdus
description: A magnificent but complex impact crater located toward the western edge of the Mare Nubium (Sea of Clouds). It stands out boldly due to its pristine, sharp structure and its complete isolation on the flat volcanic plains. Its central multi-peaked mountain system rises to more than 1.1km above the crater floor.

name: Albategnius
description: An ancient lava-filled impact crater named after the renowned 9th-century Arab astronomer and mathematician Al-Battani. Its shape is scarred by a 44km crater named Klein, which breaks through its southwestern wall.

name: Bailly
description: The largest walled plain on the Moon's visible face, located near the southwest limb. Its vast 300 km diameter spans an enormous ancient impact basin with worn and eroded features.

name: Schickard
description: A massive walled plain in the southwestern highlands featuring a relatively flat floor and eroded outer rim. Located at approximately 44.4°S and 55.1°W with a diameter of 212 km.

name: Janssen
description: A large ancient impact crater in the southeastern highlands with a diameter of 201 km. Its worn appearance and terraced inner walls indicate a very old formation from the early lunar history.

name: Humboldt
description: One of several huge rings on the lunar limb, located in the eastern highlands near the Moon's eastern edge. This 199 km diameter crater features terraced walls and stands as one of the most prominent eastern formations.

name: Maginus
description: An ancient lunar impact crater in the southern highlands, almost three-quarters the diameter of Clavius. Located southeast of Tycho, this 194 km crater features a heavily scarred surface and multiple overlapping secondary craters.

name: Petavius
description: One of the finest spots on the Moon with a grand double rampart, particularly prominent on its eastern side. This 184 km crater features numerous ridges radiating outward from its rim and stands out as a magnificent formation.

name: Longomontanus
description: A large lunar impact crater located in the southern highlands at 49.5°S and 21.7°W. This 145 km crater displays complex terraced walls and multiple central peaks characteristic of ancient highland formations.

name: Vendelinus
description: A large ancient crater in the eastern highlands featuring a complex multi-peaked central mountain range. This 147 km diameter formation shows the terraced walls typical of ancient impact structures from the early lunar period.

name: Stöfler
description: A large lunar impact crater in the southern highlands with a very level interior crossed by rays from Tycho. This 126 km crater contains at least 16 minute craters within its floor and shows ancient lunar geology.

name: Langrenus
description: A prominent crater with an irregularly terraced inner wall and wide rampart averaging about 20 kilometers across. This 132 km crater features a central peak system and is of Eratosthenian age on the lunar timescale.

name: Moretus
description: A heavily cratered impact crater near the lunar south pole featuring a prominent central mountain formation rising about 2.1 kilometers above the floor. This 114 km crater displays sharp, well-preserved features typical of younger highland impacts.

name: Russell
description: A 103 km crater located in the western Oceanus Procellarum near the lunar limb. Its proximity to the Moon's edge gives it a foreshortened appearance, making it challenging to observe from Earth due to libration effects.

name: Pitatus
description: A 101 km lava-filled crater located on the southeastern edge of Mare Nubium (Sea of Clouds). This crater features a relatively shallow floor and is surrounded by rugged highland terrain typical of the Moon's ancient southern regions.
